caption:
India just switched on a reactor that makes more fuel than it burns. It's called a breeder reactor - and it's entirely homegrown.

On April 6, 2026, India's Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, attained first criticality - becoming the country's first operational fast breeder reactor, with a 500 MWe capacity. It was designed by DAE's Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research and built by Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam, using indigenously produced Uranium-Plutonium fuel with a liquid sodium coolant and a Uranium-238 blanket to breed new fuel as it runs - a core part of India's three-stage nuclear power programme.

Most reactors just consume fuel. This one was built to make its own.

Sources: Department of Atomic Energy, Down To Earth (2026)
